title: Rapid grooming playbook: sprint-26 backfill and cut proposals
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures a rapid, defensible approach to trimming and reordering the Console & Rollouts backlog for sprint-26. This is a working artifact (notes + cut proposals + short wireframe sketches) intended to support the grooming meeting on 2026-07-13 and an asynchronous review cycle.

Goals for sprint-26 grooming:
- Free up 3-4 engineer-weeks by removing or deferring low-impact tasks.
- Lock a prioritized cut list that preserves SLAs and high-risk fixes.
- Create a fast path for 2 'swing' stories we can re-introduce if capacity allows.
- Produce minimal wireframe guidance for items that remain to avoid rework.

Participants (expected):
- Product: Ava Chen (owner), Priya Kapoor (PM lead)
- Design: Zoe Martinez
- Eng leads: Marcus Alvarez (console infra), Liam O'Neill (rollouts)
- SRE advisor (optional): Tessa Nguyen

High-level heuristics (quick filter):
1) Safety first: anything blocking SLA, security, or data isolation stays.
2) Customer impact bands: high (customer-reported regressions, enterprise blockers), medium (feature parity gaps affecting >2 teams), low (nice-to-have UX polish).
3) Implementation cost vs. unit-economics: deprioritize changes that materially increase per-token or infra cost for marginal UX gains.
4) Observability coupling: tasks that add dashboards/alerts get higher priority if they materially reduce alert noise or troubleshooting time.
5) Single-owner cleanups: small docs/rename tasks with no cross-team value -> push to backlog tidy sprint.

Backlog snapshot (selected items under evaluation):
- RI-3421: route-decision visualization overhaul (large redesign, ambiguous metrics mapping) — estimate 4w.
- RI-3550: rollout canary UI for multi-model fallback (medium complexity, customer ask) — estimate 2w.
- RI-3612: token-cost breakdown micro-ux (small; touches billing UI) — estimate 3d.
- RI-3678: onboarding quickstart wizard (large UX + infra changes) — estimate 3w.
- RI-3719: compact logs view with inline filtering (1w; high SRE request)
- RI-3748: aesthetic polish: color updates for buttons (2d)
- RI-3782: experiments: route-priority advanced JSON editor (1.5w)
- RI-3805: mobile layout fixes for metrics dashboard (1w)

Quick classification (for meeting):
- Keep (must-have): RI-3719 (logs filtering), RI-3550 (canary UI — enterprise ask), RI-3612 (token-cost breakdown, ties to billing questions).
- Swing (bring back if capacity): RI-3782 (advanced JSON editor), RI-3805 (mobile metrics).
- Defer/cut: RI-3421 (full visualization overhaul), RI-3678 (onboarding wizard), RI-3748 (aesthetic-only polish)

Rationale: RI-3421 is high cost with unclear metrics; consider extracting a tiny incremental story that adds a single metric mapping dropdown for existing view (small experiment). Onboarding wizard is product-heavy and should be decomposed into micro-acceptance steps; defer whole-bake. Aesthetic polish does not move NPS or reduce support minutes.

Proposed sprint-26 cut list (final candidates):
1) Cut: RI-3421 (visual overhaul) -> add a spike story instead: RI-3421-spike (3d) to validate metrics mapping with 2 customers.
2) Keep: RI-3550 (canary UI) -> split into two half-stories: backend routing API (1w) + UI shell + telemetry (1w).
3) Keep: RI-3719 (compact logs filter) -> prioritize as top bug fix.
4) Keep small: RI-3612 (token-cost breakdown micro-ux) -> schedule first day pair.
5) Defer: RI-3678 (onboarding wizard) -> create an epic and move to Q4 planning.
6) Defer: RI-3748 (button color polish) -> ticket to design backlog.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- RI-3550 backend: requests with model-fallback flagged appear in telemetry, canary percent toggles respect rollout policy; unit tests for fallback decisions.
- RI-3550 UI: toggle present in rollout modal, tooltip with short description, accessibility labels; e2e smoke test.
- RI-3719: filter saves query and does not regress trace performance; benchmark before/after for 90th pct latency.

Wireframe notes (quick sketches to avoid future rework):
- Canary modal: small insert below existing rollout modal. Elements: dropdown for fallback model (required), percent slider (0-100), telemetry checkbox (on by default), short inline help copy (25–30 chars). Design to reuse token-cost microcopy style.
- Compact logs: two-line per entry view with collapsible details. Inline filter chips across top with fuzzy search; default to last-24h.
- Token-cost micro-ux: small toggle in billing summary to show/hide per-route token breakdown. Use monospace alignment for numbers and a one-row sparklines cell.

Risk register (short):
- RI-3550: mis-specified fallback behavior -> risk: customer apps may see inconsistent responses. Mitigation: require toggles off by default; add e2e sim with legacy model.
- RI-3612: billing schema change risk -> mitigation: keep view-only first iteration, no writeback.

Communication plan:
- Slack summary to #console-grooming after meeting with final cut decisions and links to changed Jira statuses.
- Brief note to Solutions Engineers (SEs) for enterprise customers that expected canary UI remains prioritized.

Open questions (to resolve pre-sprint):
- Do we require legal review for any telemetry flags in RI-3550? Owner: Marcus A. Due: 2026-07-14.
- Can SRE accept an incremental logs view without re-indexing? Owner: Liam O. Due: 2026-07-14.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Ava: run grooming meeting 2026-07-13, finalize decisions and update Jira statuses.
- Priya: split RI-3550 into backend/UI tickets and add acceptance criteria (by 2026-07-14).
- Zoe: upload quick wireframe PNGs to Confluence and attach to tickets (by 2026-07-15).
- Marcus: check telemetry privacy impact and loop in legal if needed (by 2026-07-14).

Appendix: short checklist for triage reviewers
- Does this change impact per-token cost or latency? If yes, require bench notes.
- Is there a clear owner and acceptance criteria? If no, escalate to PM.
- Is there a smaller slice that delivers measurable value? Prefer slice over big-bang.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the swing bucket lean; we want optional stories we can throw into the sprint if we finish the heavy ones early.
- Avoid 'design debt' tasks unless they clear a measurable support burden.

End of doc.
